nodes.label: CQ1 deliberately-designed vs template-assembled
nodes.description: What distinguishes a site that reads as deliberately designed from one that reads as template-assembled, and which properties are machine-checkable versus human-only?

nodes.label: CQ2 layout model surviving 320-1440
nodes.description: Which layout model survives 320-1440px with no manual responsive work by the author, and what does the market record of constraint editors say?

nodes.label: CQ3 document model where the DOM is never truth
nodes.description: How must a visual editor represent its document so the DOM is never the source of truth, and what specifically breaks when it is?

nodes.label: CQ4 snap-to-gridline canvas requirements
nodes.description: What does a snap-to-gridline canvas require (gridline derivation, snap priority, tolerance divided by zoom, smart guides, grid-integer writes, keyboard parity) and what is the minimum viable version of each?

nodes.label: CQ5 which values must be derived, not picked
nodes.description: Which design-system values MUST be derived rather than picked to guarantee coherence, and what does the token standard cover including the motion/spring extension?

nodes.label: CQ6 server survival across the harness turn boundary
nodes.description: What mechanism makes a local server survive this harness turn boundary, and which pure-TypeScript candidates are proven versus assumed?

nodes.label: CQ7 concurrency protocol preventing silent work loss
nodes.description: Which concurrency protocol prevents silent work loss between an AI session and a browser editor writing the same documents?

nodes.label: CQ8 localhost design server as remote-code-drop
nodes.description: What controls stop a localhost design server from being a remote-code-drop, given DNS-rebinding-class attacks?

nodes.label: CQ9 proving zero editor runtime shipped
nodes.description: How does a build PROVE zero editor runtime shipped, is byte-reproducibility achievable on the chosen toolchain, and what is the strongest honest fallback?

nodes.label: CQ10 licence classes and per-asset metadata
nodes.description: What licence classes and per-asset metadata must be recorded for every shipped font and asset, and what does the open font licence permit for embedding, subsetting and redistribution?

nodes.label: CQ11 machine-checkable accessibility and claim wording
nodes.description: Which accessibility properties are reliably machine-checkable, what fraction of real issues does automation catch, and how must claims therefore be worded?

nodes.label: CQ12 judging motion when runtimes fight
nodes.description: How can motion quality be judged when the editor runtime fights the site runtime, and what is the state of the art including whether any validated precedent exists?

nodes.label: CQ13 ingest protocol safe against truncation and injection
nodes.description: What ingest protocol makes a manual copy-paste channel safe against BOTH silent truncation and code injection?

nodes.label: CQ14 avoiding choice overload and indistinguishability
nodes.description: How do variant systems avoid choice overload and indistinguishability, and what selection UI beats an N-up grid?

nodes.label: CQ15 undo coherence across AI bulk mutations
nodes.description: How is undo kept coherent across AI-driven bulk mutations interleaved with human edits, and where does delete-recovery belong if not in undo?

nodes.label: CQ16 warm-start split without homogenising a portfolio
nodes.description: What warm-start split preserves reuse without homogenising a portfolio, and how are prior identities injected as negative constraints?

nodes.label: CQ17 capture protocol for viewport-height layouts
nodes.description: Which capture protocol produces valid evidence for viewport-height-dependent layouts, and what makes a full-page capture invalid as hero-framing evidence?

nodes.label: CQ18 generation-channel output ceiling and chunking
nodes.description: What is the real per-message and per-conversation output ceiling on the user plan, and how does it set the chunking strategy?

nodes.label: Session
nodes.description: One run of the skill against one project: warm-start mode, asset-library path, mined sources, D1 deviations, branch choice.

nodes.label: InterviewAnswer
nodes.description: Question-ID-keyed tier-tagged answer with source (asked, pre-filled, inferred-default, skill-default) and an override flag.

nodes.label: Concept document
nodes.description: 200-300 word compression: point of view, three or more abstracted references, restraint budget, what the site refuses to do.

nodes.label: DirectionCapsule
nodes.description: Stage-A lightweight direction proposal carrying self-audit fields used by the machine pre-filter.

nodes.label: Direction
nodes.description: Fully expanded identity: 24 varying slots plus 2 invariant records, with derived values and direction-bound authored artefacts.

nodes.label: DesignToken
nodes.description: Interchange-format token with anchor-versus-derived provenance and pick and direction extension blocks.

nodes.label: SystemLock
nodes.description: Frozen system of record pinning direction id, version and per-file hashes of tokens and components.

nodes.label: ImportEnvelope
nodes.description: Declared file list, per-file line counts, sha256 prefixes, per-run terminator, quarantine records and template version.

nodes.label: Doc (scene graph)
nodes.description: Per-page document plus the project record: node tree, stable section ids, freeze flags, trash, per-breakpoint override maps.

nodes.label: Content
nodes.description: Slot-keyed copy plus the orphanage of displaced copy, separated so a content-only edit path can exist.

nodes.label: Node (component instance)
nodes.description: id, component, variant, per-breakpoint layout, props, slots, text, override, locked, notes and migration flags.

nodes.label: SlotContract
nodes.description: Typed slot definition of name, type, cardinality and required, enabling superset-only swap offers and placeholder detection.

nodes.label: Variant
nodes.description: Structurally distinct composition of one component within one direction, identified by its variant-axis vector.

nodes.label: Asset / Artwork
nodes.description: Manifest entry: lane, token-referencing flag, direction affinity, licence class, provenance, encoder settings and alt text.

nodes.label: FontCatalogEntry
nodes.description: Licence-cleared typeface with classification, foundry, source, hash, glyph coverage and pre-subsetted base64 cuts.

nodes.label: HistoryOp
nodes.description: Op-log entry with forward patch, inverse patch, transaction group id, actor and timestamp.

nodes.label: GateResult
nodes.description: Structured verdict of gate id, tier, status, measured value, threshold and evidence reference; never a thrown exception on a normal fail.

nodes.label: DirectionTourLog
nodes.description: Per-round record of directions shown, order shown, pick and stated reason, written as rounds progress.

nodes.label: EvidenceBundle
nodes.description: Fonts, assets, third-party marks, gate report, contrast proof, screenshots, direction tour, substitution log and disclosure.

nodes.label: ServerState
nodes.description: Port, pid, url and session id written at boot; the re-attach contract after a context reset.

nodes.label: Phase-0 spike suite
nodes.description: Turn-boundary, topology, font-policy, substrate, byte-reproducibility and tool-availability probes, run before dependent scope is committed.

nodes.label: Warm start
nodes.description: Glob prior systems and sites, detect an asset library, split system from identity, emit negative constraints.

nodes.label: Interview
nodes.description: Three tiers, waves of five to eight, hard gates, branching and pre-fill, producing answers and a concept document.

nodes.label: Prompt generation
nodes.description: Two-stage prompt assembly from skill-owned artefacts plus interview slots, with envelope and locally computed chunking.

nodes.label: Hand-carry and local regeneration
nodes.description: Moving a generated system across a lossy manual channel, or bypassing it with an identical-format local path.

nodes.label: Ingest and validation
nodes.description: Tolerant parsing, envelope verification, deterministic re-verification of claims, quarantine and repair-prompt emission.

nodes.label: Token compilation
nodes.description: Expanding interchange tokens into custom properties and a theme layer, compiled once per direction change.

nodes.label: Direction tournament
nodes.description: Bracketed selection with at most three full-size renders side by side and a logged reason per heat.

nodes.label: Direct manipulation
nodes.description: Snap-to-real-grid dragging that writes integers, with keyboard parity and a pre-commit breakpoint chip.

nodes.label: Variant generation
nodes.description: Deterministic, lazy, append-only expansion of a component family inside one direction, with no model call.

nodes.label: Scoped regeneration
nodes.description: Note-driven regeneration of one section, executed inline, committed as a single undo step.

nodes.label: Migration
nodes.description: Remapping references after a system change; unmappable nodes are listed explicitly and never silently dropped.

nodes.label: LOCK
nodes.description: Build, scrub, assert, snapshot and tag: a re-render with the editor disabled that writes only the published tree and the snapshot directory.

nodes.label: Publish
nodes.description: Automated static deploy after one-time credential setup, or an emitted runbook fallback that does not satisfy the exit criterion.

nodes.label: Evidence bundling
nodes.description: Assembling licence, gate, contrast, capture, tour and substitution records with an explicit non-conformance disclosure.

nodes.label: Resume
nodes.description: Recomputing the pipeline phase from disk and re-attaching to a live server rather than relaunching it.

nodes.label: Anti-slop lint as an upstream hard gate
nodes.description: Lint the generated design-system JSON before the human sees the menu; demote to a dismissible advisory at the human-edit layer.

nodes.label: Bracketed tournament selection
nodes.description: Three shown, pick, three shown, pick, head-to-head; roughly six of ten surfaced by default with a see-more path.

nodes.label: Signature moment as a bespoke concept
nodes.description: Two or three bespoke concept candidates per direction rather than a catalogue pick; a lint flags a second signature moment.

nodes.label: Human as sole aesthetic judge
nodes.description: No AI aesthetic scoring anywhere; machines enforce only machine-checkable correctness and may refuse a correctness violation.

nodes.label: Reference triangulation from three or more sources
nodes.description: Each direction abstracts references from different eras, genres and cultures; regenerate if any single reference overlaps beyond the stated share.

nodes.label: Four-level layout contract
nodes.description: Page is a reorder-only list of sections; section is a real grid; block is integer placement; inside a block is flow only.

nodes.label: Desktop-down cascade with sparse overrides
nodes.description: Author at the desktop key; overrides attach downward only; never two independent layouts.

nodes.label: Full-bleed small-breakpoint default
nodes.description: A node with no small-key entry compiles to a full-width placement in source order, preventing the documented overlap epidemic.

nodes.label: Container queries inside components
nodes.description: Inline-size containment on every block wrapper so component internals key off the space they were dropped into, not the viewport.

nodes.label: Grid-integer placement from computed styles
nodes.description: Read resolved tracks, round the pointer to a column line, persist start and span so six of twelve is fifty percent at every width.

nodes.label: Normative drop algorithm
nodes.description: Row derivation from a spacing-scale row unit, span preservation with clamping, displace-down occupancy with ghost preview, cross-section re-parenting without compaction.

nodes.label: Named areas with per-block promotion
nodes.description: Ship section archetypes as named areas; promote only the dragged block to explicit integers on the same grid.

nodes.label: DOM order is the reading order
nodes.description: Visual order comes only from grid placement; a per-breakpoint order override is hard-blocked on focusable nodes and warned elsewhere.

nodes.label: Numbered mobile stack-order preview
nodes.description: Before any commit that changes mobile stacking, render the resulting top-to-bottom sequence as a numbered list.

nodes.label: Two-tier truth
nodes.description: Composition documents are the only thing the editor mutates; implementation files are versioned; the rendered site is never parsed back.

nodes.label: Total pure renderer
nodes.description: Render is a pure, total function of document, system lock and library; every reference resolves or the migration policy fires.

nodes.label: Typed semantic ops
nodes.description: The browser and the agent post typed ops; a raw patch or a file path in a request body is rejected.

nodes.label: Annotation scoped by descent
nodes.description: Annotate once at the node boundary and inherit for descendants; emit annotations only in design mode and assert their absence at lock.

nodes.label: Zero DOM injection for hit-testing
nodes.description: Hit-test attributes on elements that already exist plus one sibling overlay outside the layout root; lock removes one element and one script.

nodes.label: Canonical document serialisation
nodes.description: Fixed key order, two-space indent, one array element per line, shortest round-trip numbers, absent optional keys omitted.

nodes.label: Gridline overlay from computed styles
nodes.description: Paint the exact resolved tracks read from the section; never a decorative grid; the overlay lives outside the preview frame.

nodes.label: Prioritised snap interval index
nodes.description: Two one-dimensional interval indexes per section over grid lines, sibling edges and centres, padding and content rails, and spacing-scale increments.

nodes.label: Snap tolerance divided by zoom
nodes.description: A six to eight pixel tolerance divided by the zoom factor so snapping stays usable at both extremes of the zoom range.

nodes.label: Smart guides with distance labels
nodes.description: Dashed guides plus live gap measurements and equal-spacing indicators when three or more siblings match.

nodes.label: Keyboard nudge and grid stepping
nodes.description: Arrow moves one cell, shift-arrow changes span, tab walks siblings; this is the single-pointer alternative for every drag.

nodes.label: Pre-commit breakpoint chip
nodes.description: A persistent chip naming exactly which sizes an edit affects, with one-click apply-to-all, plus overridden-here dots and reset.

nodes.label: Anchored-offset free positioning
nodes.description: Not raw absolute: a declared anchor plus a proportional or clamped offset; v1 anchors are parent edge or grid cell only.

nodes.label: Authored flow fallback with auto-demote
nodes.description: Free-positioned nodes carry an authored fallback used below the demotion width; a reserved minimum block size prevents parent collapse.

nodes.label: Free-position and overlap counters
nodes.description: Per-section caps with a visible counter for free-positioned blocks and for opt-in overlap pairs.

nodes.label: Derived-value computation from anchors
nodes.description: Spacing, type steps, radius, shadow, semantic roles, state layers and font-fallback metrics are computed from the vector plus seed tables.

nodes.label: Frozen token-name manifest
nodes.description: A closed list of token name paths generated mechanically and re-pasted verbatim, so no model invents or renames a key.

nodes.label: Per-direction validity lists
nodes.description: Repickable rows ship a validity list; options outside the active direction are hidden from the interface, not merely warned about.

nodes.label: Flat variable layer per direction change
nodes.description: Compile the full custom-property set once per direction change instead of re-resolving hundreds of properties per drag.

nodes.label: Agreed motion and spring token extension
nodes.description: Springs sit outside the interchange standard, so every tool must agree one extension shape or motion degrades to none.

nodes.label: One container contract for art and motion
nodes.description: Aspect policy, anchor, scheme awareness, reduced-motion references, typed trigger, source, playback, cost class and token references in one shape.

nodes.label: Turn-boundary survival probe
nodes.description: Launch, same-turn success, end the turn, re-check in a separate call and confirm the recorded pid is still alive, repeated across boundaries and a context clear.

nodes.label: Launcher fallback ladder
nodes.description: Detached spawn, double fork, shell launcher, sign-off-gated shim, user-run terminal; take the first passing rung.

nodes.label: Fixed port plus state record re-attach
nodes.description: Fixed loopback port, boot-time state record, retrying health check to confirm bind, regenerate-if-stale on startup.

nodes.label: Second health check in a separate tool call
nodes.description: The only accepted proof of server liveness; a same-turn success proves binding, not survival.

nodes.label: Idle shutdown
nodes.description: The server retires itself so two processes do not become two things to forget to shut down.

nodes.label: Event stream plus append-only inbox with a blocking read
nodes.description: Browser requests land in an append-only inbox picked up by a blocking read, costing zero tokens while the user designs.

nodes.label: Single-writer ownership
nodes.description: One server process writes the document-owned set; the browser and the agent only propose ops.

nodes.label: Hash-journal reconciliation
nodes.description: A journal of path, hash, mtime and sequence plus a watch; an unexplained hash change becomes a visible conflict with both versions retained.

nodes.label: Optimistic concurrency with a conflict status
nodes.description: A stale validator or hash mismatch is rejected with a conflict status and the editor offers reload or force.

nodes.label: Process lock plus event-stream tab claim
nodes.description: A pid lock covers processes; a stream-based claim covers tabs, with the second tab read-only.

nodes.label: Sanctioned agent write path
nodes.description: The agent changes a page by posting a typed op through the same server, never by writing the document file.

nodes.label: Fail-open ownership guard hook
nodes.description: A cheap pre-tool guard blocking writes to document-owned paths while the lock is held; a heuristic, defeatable, and stated as such.

nodes.label: Six-control localhost posture
nodes.description: Loopback binding, origin allowlist, bearer token, semantic-op wire format, path allowlist and idle shutdown.

nodes.label: Resolved-path prefix assertion
nodes.description: Every write path is resolved and prefix-asserted; a symlinked path is rejected.

nodes.label: LOCK as re-render, never copy-and-strip
nodes.description: Same renderer with the editor disabled; the first-party copy-and-strip precedent required hand-rewriting links and excluding development pages.

nodes.label: Two configs, two commands, two output directories
nodes.description: Only the design configuration registers the editor integration, so the editor is not in the publish build graph at all.

nodes.label: Eight purity gates
nodes.description: Editor-string grep, two-build equality, script size step, screenshot diff, interaction manifest, zero unresolved references, zero design-time origins, verify clean.

nodes.label: Manifest-based two-build comparison
nodes.description: Clean worktree, committed editor-free dependency set, pinned epoch, locale, timezone and runtime, compared by sorted path plus per-file hash.

nodes.label: Normalised-comparison fallback
nodes.description: Identical file list and hashes except a named, enumerated, justified exception set; weakens the proof and requires sign-off.

nodes.label: Deterministic generation
nodes.description: Frozen clock, sorted keys, relative paths, fixed collator, stable identifiers, pinned asset encoder and no ambient inputs.

nodes.label: Verify by regenerate-and-diff
nodes.description: Regenerate into a temporary directory and diff text files, hash-comparing binaries separately; an empty diff proves determinism and no hand-edits.

nodes.label: Write-to-new-directory-then-swap export
nodes.description: Export never deletes recursively; the new tree is built alongside and swapped.

nodes.label: Asset manifest as the reference allowlist
nodes.description: Every asset reference validates against the manifest, so a hallucinated or stale path fails loudly at generate time rather than serving a broken file.

nodes.label: Pre-subsetted licence-cleared font catalog
nodes.description: Base64 cuts computed locally once and pasted verbatim, so the generation channel never invents a face declaration or a family.

nodes.label: Commercial-foundry pre-launch blocker
nodes.description: A commercial face emits a blocker rather than being embedded.

nodes.label: Third-party marks used as supplied
nodes.description: Platform badges, social icons, trust badges and map tiles are deterministic embeds, never redrawn by a generator.

nodes.label: Scoped accessibility engine runs
nodes.description: Run the rule engine on the touched subtree live and the full ruleset at lock; scoped runs are natively supported.

nodes.label: Second-ruleset cross-check
nodes.description: A second independent ruleset raises coverage without claiming completeness.

nodes.label: Dual contrast gate
nodes.description: Pass the legally standing ratio test and compute the perceptual model as a stricter internal target; both are two-colour arithmetic.

nodes.label: Scripted keyboard tab-walk
nodes.description: Focus order matches visual order, no traps, a visible ring at every stop, nothing obscured; runs after the skip-link gate.

nodes.label: Fixed disclosure wording
nodes.description: Report the passed automated gate count plus an explicit manual-and-screen-reader-review-not-performed line; never a conformance claim.

nodes.label: Motion disabled in edit mode
nodes.description: The editor runtime and the site runtime cannot share the page, so motion is judged in preview; this is the unsolved part.

nodes.label: Deterministic motion lint
nodes.description: Static checks for non-compositor properties, out-of-band durations and a missing reduced-motion query.

nodes.label: Art-directed reduced-motion siblings
nodes.description: Every motion-capable container references a tagged reduced variant authored at generation time, never derived by zeroing duration.

nodes.label: Live motion-concurrency counter
nodes.description: Recount heavy and gpu cost-class instances on every placement so the count accumulates visibly instead of surfacing at lock.

nodes.label: Pause, stop and hide affordance contract
nodes.description: Every continuous-motion container resolves a non-null pause affordance reference that is keyboard-operable.

nodes.label: Envelope manifest with a per-run terminator
nodes.description: Declared file list, per-file line counts, hash prefixes, smallest-first ordering and a random terminator make truncation detectable.

nodes.label: Tolerant fenced-block parser
nodes.description: Split on file-header blocks and validate against the envelope rather than trusting the channel.

nodes.label: Quarantine and repair-prompt emission
nodes.description: Security rejections are quarantined and reported per item; nothing is partially applied and a repair prompt is emitted.

nodes.label: Syntax-tree walk for forbidden interfaces
nodes.description: Flag network, clock, randomness and environment reads in imported components at import time.

nodes.label: Deterministic re-verification of claims
nodes.description: Recompute every claimed contrast pair and licence claim locally instead of trusting the generated declaration.

nodes.label: Local regeneration mode
nodes.description: The identical prompt executed locally, producing identical-format output with zero pastes, making the web hop a preference.

nodes.label: Bounded-paste protocol
nodes.description: One paste per chunk as the mechanism with a retry budget; each extra paste is logged as a near-miss.

nodes.label: Empirical chunk sizing
nodes.description: Compute chunk sizes from measured artifact sizes at runtime rather than from any published ceiling.

nodes.label: Up-front usage-tier disclosure
nodes.description: Surface the plan cost of a two-stage generation across many directions before the user starts.

nodes.label: Lazy per-direction variant generation
nodes.description: Generate on first open of a family panel, cache per direction, never pre-generate families the site does not use.

nodes.label: Variant axis vector
nodes.description: Every component declares an axis vector; two variants are structurally distinct if their vectors differ in at least one axis.

nodes.label: Thumbnail indistinguishability rule
nodes.description: No two variants offered in the same bar may be indistinguishable at the stated thumbnail size.

nodes.label: In-context hover preview
nodes.description: Ghost-preview a variant in the real slot with current copy and neighbours; an isolated thumbnail cannot show fit.

nodes.label: Direction-affinity filter chips
nodes.description: Filter an artwork set by direction affinity; the chips are what makes presenting twenty pieces legal.

nodes.label: Superset-only swap offers
nodes.description: Offer only variants whose slot contract is a superset or exact match, and state added and unhousable slots before the swap.

nodes.label: Content orphanage
nodes.description: Copy the target cannot hold is parked visibly, never deleted, and auto-restored when a later swap re-introduces the slot.

nodes.label: Placeholders that block LOCK
nodes.description: Newly created empty slots render as flagged placeholders that block lock until filled or deleted, which is what prevents fake statistics shipping.

nodes.label: Single command stack
nodes.description: One patch stack over the document covering canvas, inspector and text edits, mirroring the server-authoritative op log.

nodes.label: Transactional grouping
nodes.description: A swap or a regeneration is one undo step; naive per-mutation undo leaves a broken hybrid exactly when the safety net matters.

nodes.label: Append-only op log with inverse patches
nodes.description: Each entry carries the forward and inverse patch, so undo survives a reload and doubles as an agent-versus-human audit trail.

nodes.label: Recovery bin independent of undo
nodes.description: Deleting three edits ago is common, and chaining undo back would revert everything since, so recovery is a separate store.

nodes.label: Milestone-only commits
nodes.description: Commit at lock, import, migration, checkpoint and session end; durability between milestones is the op log plus atomic writes.

nodes.label: Warm start as a glob
nodes.description: Discover prior systems and sites with a glob over known library paths rather than new infrastructure.

nodes.label: System-versus-identity split
nodes.description: Carry forward schema, contracts, primitives, catalog, deny-list and configuration; never carry hues, pairings, density, motion character, artwork or the signature moment.

nodes.label: Prior identity as negative constraints
nodes.description: Inject prior hues and pairings as things to avoid unless the user declares the new site a sibling.

nodes.label: Forced-divergence axis assignment
nodes.description: Assign each generated direction a position on a divergence axis so ten directions do not all regress to the mean.

nodes.label: Device-height pinning
nodes.description: Pin both the preview frame and the capture window to a real device size whenever the page contains a viewport-height rule.

nodes.label: Assert the measured preview height
nodes.description: Measure and assert the achieved height rather than assuming a viewport configuration was honoured.

nodes.label: Dependency-free headless capture
nodes.description: Plain browser command-line headless capture with a non-empty-output assertion and zero package dependencies.

nodes.label: Capture wait recipe
nodes.description: Navigate rather than set content, network idle with a load fallback, strip lazy loading, fonts ready plus per-image decode, deferred style settle.

nodes.label: Same-origin preview frame
nodes.description: A scaled element cannot evaluate media queries against a simulated width; a frame can, because its own viewport is what queries see.

nodes.label: Explicit migration report
nodes.description: Map old references to new, list unmappable nodes, and require the user to resolve each; logged as an operation, not a side effect.

nodes.label: Reviewed direction application
nodes.description: Applying a new direction flags every affected node, blocks lock until acknowledged, and offers bulk acknowledge.

nodes.label: Versioned coherence lint set
nodes.description: Includes the elevation-model lint, the logical-properties-only lint and the artefact-versus-vector lints; the count is versioned, not fixed.

nodes.label: Logical properties only
nodes.description: Emit inline and block logical properties everywhere and never physical directions; enforced at ingest and at lock.

nodes.label: Build-time vector charts
nodes.description: Pre-render charts with a small mark-type cap so no chart runtime ships and only truthful data states are published.

nodes.label: Derived data-visualisation sub-tokens
nodes.description: Categorical, sequential and diverging ramps derived from the direction anchors and validated colourblind-safe in both schemes.

nodes.label: Phase recomputed from disk
nodes.description: Resume reads the frontier from artifacts on disk and never relies on conversation memory.

nodes.label: Re-attach, never relaunch
nodes.description: After a context clear the resume instruction points at the recorded port and pid rather than starting a second server.

nodes.label: Symlink installation
nodes.description: Install the skill as a symlink to the tracked copy so the duplicate-copies drift pattern cannot repeat.

nodes.label: Structured gate verdicts
nodes.description: Gates return a verdict object with measured value and threshold and never throw on a normal fail.

nodes.label: Inline role-prompt execution
nodes.description: Role prompts run in the main session with already-declared tools, so nothing depends on unverified mid-skill subagent availability.

nodes.label: Phase-zero confirmation gate
nodes.description: Restate the understood brief and wait for an explicit yes before any file write or server launch.

nodes.label: Machine-detectable slop tells
nodes.description: Count of catalogued tells present in a generated design system; a large page analysis found a majority carrying at least one signature.

nodes.label: Distinct motion kinds in use
nodes.description: Count of distinct motion kinds deployed per site; a soft advisory fires at three or more variants of the same kind.

nodes.label: Stated reason recorded per heat
nodes.description: Whether every tournament heat recorded the pick and the stated reason; the qualitative basis of the traceability goal.

nodes.label: Reflow findings at the narrowest width
nodes.description: Two-dimensional scroll findings at 320 pixels, excluding exempted content.

nodes.label: Document overflow assertion
nodes.description: Scroll width against client width at every checked width; free-positioned elements get mandatory extra scrutiny.

nodes.label: Free-positioned blocks per section
nodes.description: Visible counter against a per-section cap; the same lint family counts opt-in overlap pairs.

nodes.label: Overlay-versus-computed track match
nodes.description: Overlay track positions must equal the resolved template columns exactly.

nodes.label: Snap usability across zoom
nodes.description: Snapping remains usable at both extremes of the zoom range because tolerance is divided by zoom.

nodes.label: Target-size violations
nodes.description: Interactive elements below the minimum target size without a documented exception, checked live on render and swept at lock.

nodes.label: Verify diff emptiness
nodes.description: The regenerate-to-temporary diff must be empty on a fresh project and after ten drag operations.

nodes.label: Canonical serialisation diff
nodes.description: Re-serialising every document into canonical form must produce a zero diff, so a foreign serialiser cannot lock.

nodes.label: Resolved tokens per direction
nodes.description: A budget of roughly six hundred to nine hundred resolved tokens per complete direction, counted programmatically from shipped systems.

nodes.label: Derived-token control coverage
nodes.description: Share of derived tokens exposing no editor control; must be total.

nodes.label: Post-turn-boundary health status
nodes.description: Status returned by a health request issued in a separate tool call after the turn boundary.

nodes.label: Recorded process liveness
nodes.description: Whether the process recorded at boot is still present after each boundary, including across a context clear.

nodes.label: Out-of-band writes surfaced
nodes.description: Count of journal mismatches surfaced as conflicts with both versions retained; silent overwrites must be zero.

nodes.label: Stale saves rejected
nodes.description: Every stale save is rejected with a conflict status and surfaces a reload-or-force choice.

nodes.label: Origin and token rejections
nodes.description: Requests from a non-allowlisted origin or without the session token are rejected on every mutating route and on the event stream.

nodes.label: Symlinked path rejections
nodes.description: Writes outside the allowlist, including via symlink, are rejected after path resolution.

nodes.label: Editor strings in the published tree
nodes.description: Grep count of editor attributes, development toolbar markers, client shims and source-location attributes; must be zero.

nodes.label: Two-build manifest equality
nodes.description: Sorted path list plus per-file hash must be identical between the editor-installed and editor-free builds.

nodes.label: Published script byte size
nodes.description: A step change in shipped script size exposes an accidental editor import.

nodes.label: Editor-versus-built screenshot delta
nodes.description: A capture of the chrome-hidden editor preview and of the built page at the same width must differ by zero pixels.

nodes.label: Unresolved reference count
nodes.description: Component, variant, motion, asset and token references that do not resolve, plus unacknowledged migration flags; failure lists nodes.

nodes.label: Design-time origins in output
nodes.description: Occurrences of loopback hosts, file URLs, the session port or the session root path anywhere in emitted output; must be zero.

nodes.label: Licence-class coverage
nodes.description: Share of shipped fonts and assets carrying a recorded licence class; must be total, and is build-failing.

nodes.label: Asset-reference resolution
nodes.description: Every url, family, vector identifier reference and asset path in built output resolves to a manifest entry and a real file, with zero remote hosts.

nodes.label: Critical and serious findings
nodes.description: The full-page rule-engine sweep must report zero critical and zero serious findings.

nodes.label: Contrast ratio per pairing
nodes.description: Normal text, large text and non-text ratios computed for every touched pair and swept at lock.

nodes.label: Perceptual contrast value per pairing
nodes.description: An advisory stricter target computed alongside the legal ratio; the specific bands are inherited and not re-verified.

nodes.label: Automated accessibility coverage share
nodes.description: Roughly fifty-seven percent of real issues caught by automated testing across thirteen thousand page-states.

nodes.label: Motion instances by cost class
nodes.description: Live and lock-time counts of gpu and heavy cost-class containers per page against the provisional caps.

nodes.label: Model recall of aesthetic animation
nodes.description: Measured low in prior work that flags the area as unvalidated end to end; the reason no automated visual score is trusted.

nodes.label: Ingest refusals on envelope mismatch
nodes.description: A truncated or mismatched chunk must fail naming the missing files and write no partial system.

nodes.label: Quarantined items per import
nodes.description: Items rejected for a forbidden interface, recorded per item with reason and offending snippet.

nodes.label: Pastes per chunk
nodes.description: Ingest invocations per chunk against a retry budget of three; each extra paste is a logged near-miss.

nodes.label: Chunks per generation cycle
nodes.description: Number of chunks required per cycle against a target ceiling of six.

nodes.label: Indistinguishable variant pairs
nodes.description: Pairs offered in the same bar that are visually indistinguishable at thumbnail size; must be zero.

nodes.label: Directions surfaced versus generated
nodes.description: Roughly six surfaced by default from about ten generated, with the rest available on demand.

nodes.label: Variants per component family
nodes.description: Ten per swappable family and twelve for the six with the largest surface-by-frequency product, generated lazily.

nodes.label: Bulk mutation undo granularity
nodes.description: A swap and a section regeneration must each restore completely with one undo, leaving no hybrid state.

nodes.label: Hue distance from prior identities
nodes.description: Generated directions must avoid a stated angular neighbourhood of prior hue anchors unless the site is declared a sibling.

nodes.label: Single-reference overlap share
nodes.description: A direction overlapping any one reference beyond the stated share is regenerated against a different reference.

nodes.label: Capture matrix completeness
nodes.description: Screenshots across the checked widths by scheme by motion state, including pinned-device-height captures.

nodes.label: Measured preview height
nodes.description: The achieved preview height is measured and asserted rather than assumed from configuration.

nodes.label: Core web vitals and pre-render transfer
nodes.description: Load, stability and responsiveness metrics under a documented throttling profile plus the pre-render transfer budget.

nodes.label: Lock wall-clock time
nodes.description: Target median and tail durations for a representative multi-page site; an inference sized against the expanded gate list, not measured.

nodes.label: Override accumulation
nodes.description: Overrides per page and per site against stated starting thresholds; a heavily overridden page stops being a design-system site.

nodes.label: Interview elapsed time
nodes.description: Wall-clock duration; fast mode is estimated at twenty-five to thirty-five minutes, a projection requiring instrumentation.

nodes.label: Questions asked versus bank size
nodes.description: Roughly forty-five to fifty-five tier-one questions asked in fast mode out of a ninety-question bank.

nodes.label: Completed lock events per project per window
nodes.description: Counted from local session files inside a rolling ninety-day window, with no telemetry and no backend.

nodes.label: Font-swap attributable layout shift
nodes.description: Layout shift attributable to font swap measured via a shift-source breakdown rather than the aggregate number.

nodes.label: Skip link presence and first tab stop
nodes.description: A working skip link exists, is the first tab stop, and moves focus into the main landmark.

nodes.label: Pause affordance resolution
nodes.description: Every continuous-motion container resolves a non-null, keyboard-operable pause control.

nodes.label: Structured-data and metadata completeness
nodes.description: Unique titles, description length, canonical, social tags, language, single top heading, alt coverage, sitemap and validated structured data.

nodes.label: Script-disabled render usability
nodes.description: Content visible, navigation usable and forms submittable with scripting disabled; also the crawler view.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.2 AA
nodes.description: The contractual accessibility floor and the pass/fail gate for this product.

nodes.label: Dragging Movements (AA)
nodes.description: All functionality using a dragging movement must be achievable by a single pointer without dragging unless dragging is essential; applies to the editor itself.

nodes.label: Target Size (AA)
nodes.description: A minimum target size with four exceptions; award-style editor chrome violates this by default.

nodes.label: Bypass Blocks (A)
nodes.description: A working skip link, present and first in tab order, jumping past repeated chrome into main content.

nodes.label: Pause, Stop, Hide (A)
nodes.description: Unconditional wherever continuous motion runs beyond five seconds alongside other content.

nodes.label: Focus Order (A)
nodes.description: Why a per-breakpoint order override is hard-blocked on focusable nodes.

nodes.label: Meaningful Sequence (A)
nodes.description: Why reordering non-focusable content warns rather than blocks, with the warning as the record of deliberateness.

nodes.label: Reflow (AA)
nodes.description: No two-dimensional scroll at the narrowest checked width except exempted content.

nodes.label: Non-text Contrast (AA)
nodes.description: Non-text contrast swept alongside text contrast at lock.

nodes.label: Text Spacing (AA)
nodes.description: An override stylesheet stress applied to a scoped clone and at lock.

nodes.label: Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A)
nodes.description: A conditional photosensitivity scan on strobe or glitch tagged assets.

nodes.label: Motion Actuation (A)
nodes.description: A conditional check that device-orientation-driven behaviour has an interface alternative and is disableable.

nodes.label: Status Messages (AA)
nodes.description: The contract behind the shared live-region announcer primitive.

nodes.label: Content on Hover or Focus (AA)
nodes.description: The contract behind the non-modal popup primitive covering hover overlays.

nodes.label: Perceptual contrast model (draft)
nodes.description: A candidate for the next accessibility guideline generation, still draft, with no independent legal standing today; advisory only.

nodes.label: Reduced-motion user preference
nodes.description: The preference every motion-capable container must honour with an art-directed sibling, not a zeroed duration.

nodes.label: Design-token interchange format
nodes.description: The token shape the generated system must conform to, with motion springs as an out-of-standard extension.

nodes.label: JSON Patch (RFC 6902)
nodes.description: The representation of forward and inverse patches in the op log.

nodes.label: Conditional requests and conflict semantics
nodes.description: Validator-based optimistic concurrency and conflict reporting on document writes.

nodes.label: SHA-256
nodes.description: Envelope verification, per-file build manifests, document hash journaling and asset derivation pinning.

nodes.label: Reproducible-build environment pinning
nodes.description: A frozen clock plus pinned timezone, locale and runtime version so two builds are comparable at all.

nodes.label: Open font licence terms
nodes.description: What may be embedded, subsetted and redistributed, and what attribution is required.

nodes.label: Third-party mark usage rules
nodes.description: Platform badges and social icons must be used as supplied; generating one is a trademark violation.

nodes.label: Look-and-feel and trade-dress practice
nodes.description: Look and feel is largely not copyrightable absent confusion plus an integrated non-functional claim, hence triangulation from three or more references.

nodes.label: Localhost rebinding attack class
nodes.description: The recorded vulnerability class establishing that a loopback bind is not a trust boundary.

nodes.label: Generation-surface content security policy
nodes.description: The policy that admits a stylesheet but restricts font sources, which is why typography cannot be judged where directions are chosen.

nodes.label: Generation-surface product limits
nodes.description: Vendor-described behaviour of the artifact surface, including one live artifact per turn; someone else's product surface and subject to change.

nodes.label: Structured-data vocabulary
nodes.description: Structured-data types matched to the site-type answer and validated.

nodes.label: Core web vitals thresholds
nodes.description: Load, stability and responsiveness bands at the seventy-fifth percentile; the responsiveness metric replaced its predecessor in 2024.

nodes.label: Baseline platform availability
nodes.description: Container queries, relational selectors, registered properties, cascade layers, nesting and logical properties are widely available; subgrid is universal; anchor positioning is not yet safe for load-bearing layout.

nodes.label: ARIA authoring practices patterns
nodes.description: The behaviour source of truth for pattern-mapped components; their variants are skin-only.

nodes.label: Agent harness execution contract
nodes.description: Turn-boundary reaping, working-directory resets, absent timeout binary, permission scoring, subagent write restrictions and context-clear behaviour.

nodes.label: Skill and agent contract
nodes.description: Frontmatter shape, tool declaration authority, no new agent definitions, and skill precedence.

nodes.label: Standing language rule
nodes.description: New code is TypeScript run by Bun, with no new Python except an explicitly sign-off-gated launcher rung.

nodes.label: R1 artwork undeliverable from the generation channel
nodes.description: No raster generation, so a twenty-artwork ask returns flat geometric vectors in the exact slop register.

nodes.label: R2 typefaces unrenderable where directions are chosen
nodes.description: The generation surface blocks the font binary, so the user picks a look they have never seen.

nodes.label: R3 silent truncation produces valid but wrong output
nodes.description: A truncated payload is syntactically fine and renders, so a partial system is accepted with no error anywhere.

nodes.label: R4 DOM as source of truth
nodes.description: Round-tripping rendered markup is lossy exactly where anchors, variants and intent live, and worse when an agent also writes the source.

nodes.label: R5 servers reaped at the turn boundary
nodes.description: First-party verified across four documented attempts; the failure appears intermittent because it depends on turn timing.

nodes.label: R6 two writers with no lock
nodes.description: The product design encourages alternating between conversation and dragging, making silent work loss near-certain.

nodes.label: R7 hand-carry cost and loop
nodes.description: A long manual cycle that step five turns into a loop; the most likely quiet death of the product.

nodes.label: R8 the constraint editor is the one that died
nodes.description: The closest commercial analogue was sunset; moving an element a small distance is a four-way puzzle under constraint layout.

nodes.label: R9 free position does not degrade gracefully
nodes.description: It collapses parents and bakes in the authoring viewport, and nothing breaks until the site is opened on a phone weeks later.

nodes.label: R12 language-rule gravity
nodes.description: An existing estate of prior-language scripts pulls new work away from the standing language rule.

nodes.label: R13 no asset library means no real artwork
nodes.description: A project with no asset library gets code-drawn art only, and a whole branch of the design system becomes dead weight.

nodes.label: R14 editor runtime fights site runtime
nodes.description: Motion feel cannot be judged while editing; disabling motion in edit mode is the only workable answer and it creates the problem.

nodes.label: R15 determinism false positives
nodes.description: A verify step that cries wolf teaches users to ignore it and the drift guarantee dies silently.

nodes.label: R16 localhost is not a trust boundary
nodes.description: A recorded vulnerability class shows loopback services reachable from hostile pages.

nodes.label: R17 ingest is an unauthenticated code-import channel
nodes.description: The payload is evaluated by the development server and bundled into the published site.

nodes.label: R18 scope is several products
nodes.description: The canvas layer alone is a multi-year multi-team category; all effort figures are inference.

nodes.label: R19 editor and export divergence
nodes.description: Without a screenshot-diff gate the shipped page can differ from the approved surface with no visible cause.

nodes.label: R20 month-six rot
nodes.description: The first-party precedent already rotted: unversioned tree, opaque variant directories, no manifest, builder source in a temporary directory.

nodes.label: R21 the interview spends the user's time worst
nodes.description: A long bank precedes any pixel, followed by direction review and many component decisions.

nodes.label: R22 undo fractures across bulk mutations
nodes.description: A naive per-mutation stack leaves a broken hybrid after a single undo.

nodes.label: R23 invented third-party marks
nodes.description: A generator will draw a platform badge, which is a trademark violation rather than a design choice.

nodes.label: R24 charts break coherence by construction
nodes.description: A three-hue brand cannot yield a six-series colourblind-safe categorical palette without derived sub-tokens.

nodes.label: R26 warm start homogenises the portfolio
nodes.description: Site two becomes a recolour of site one, invisible until there are three sites.

nodes.label: R27 the editor caps the quality ceiling
nodes.description: A swap menu is template assembly; the promise must be calibrated and a bespoke escape hatch reserved.

nodes.label: R28 directions regress to the mean
nodes.description: Ten directions generated without forced-divergence constraints converge.

nodes.label: R29 eager variant generation stalls selection
nodes.description: Generating every family's variants up front is a large wasted cost at the exact moment the user is waiting.

nodes.label: R30 per-drag custom-property re-evaluation
nodes.description: Hundreds of custom properties re-resolved per drag is a real reflow cost.

nodes.label: R31 motion variants are the least verifiable inventory
nodes.description: Automated recall of aesthetic animation is poor, so acceptance rests on the human plus deterministic lint.

nodes.label: R33 undifferentiated variants
nodes.description: Variants that cannot be told apart at thumbnail size reproduce the choice-overload failure.

nodes.label: R34 twenty artworks exceed the presentation ceiling
nodes.description: Without affinity filter chips a twenty-piece set is unusable as a chooser.

nodes.label: R36 pasted source-app markup survives export
nodes.description: Rich text carried from another application pollutes an award-grade type system.

nodes.label: R41 deploy is a second manual boundary
nodes.description: If publish is not automated, every future content edit ends in a dashboard upload.

nodes.label: R44 the prompt is a lottery ticket, not a build artifact
nodes.description: Generation output is non-deterministic and the model drifts, so the result must be persisted as the artifact of record.

nodes.label: R45 transformed art containers trap overlays
nodes.description: A transformed ancestor creates a containing block that traps dropdowns behind artwork.

nodes.label: R47 D2 unexercised at first ship
nodes.description: Retired by the decision to pull the canvas into the first shipping version, at the cost of front-loading the riskiest mechanic.

nodes.label: Single-writer server pattern
nodes.description: One process owns a file set; every other actor proposes typed operations through it.

nodes.label: Event stream plus append-only inbox
nodes.description: A proven in-estate pattern for zero-token human-in-the-loop waiting across three existing servers.

nodes.label: Machine-owned versus human-owned split
nodes.description: Regenerated files are never hand-edited; a scaffolded wrapper is never touched again by the generator.

nodes.label: Annotate once, inherit by descent
nodes.description: A node-boundary annotation scopes all descendants, so mapping needs no instrumentation pass.

nodes.label: Chrome outside the preview frame
nodes.description: Handles, rings, guides and gridlines live in a sibling overlay so removal at lock is provably a no-op.

nodes.label: Append-only indices
nodes.description: New variants take the next index from a skill-supplied high-water mark so numbering never collides with prior imports.

nodes.label: Frontier recomputed from disk
nodes.description: State is derived from artifacts rather than memory, which is what makes resume trustworthy.

nodes.label: Structured verdict, never an exception
nodes.description: Quality checks return data with measured values and thresholds so a normal failure is reportable rather than fatal.

nodes.label: Symlink distribution
nodes.description: A single tracked copy linked into the global location, breaking the duplicate-copy drift pattern already observed in the estate.

nodes.label: Write new, then swap
nodes.description: Destructive removal is replaced by building alongside and swapping, which also avoids a high-friction permission prompt.

nodes.label: HTML to JSON round-tripping
nodes.description: The canonical editor failure: parse, edit, re-serialise, and lose comments, formatting and intent.

nodes.label: Injected wrappers for hit-testing
nodes.description: Wrappers change what child and sibling selectors match, so removing them at lock silently shifts layout.

nodes.label: Decorative gridlines
nodes.description: An overlay that is not the real grid makes snapping cosmetic and makes a later grid change reflow nothing.

nodes.label: Two independent per-breakpoint layouts
nodes.description: A separate mobile grid with independent placement produced a documented overlap epidemic in a shipped product.

nodes.label: Raw absolute positioning as free position
nodes.description: It leaves flow, collapses the parent, and bakes in the authoring viewport width.

nodes.label: Flattened style-by-motion variant list
nodes.description: Presenting the full combinatorial product as one list is unusable; the picker must stay two independent tabs.

nodes.label: N-up direction grid
nodes.description: Thumbnail grids systematically favour loud, high-contrast directions over subtle editorial ones.

nodes.label: Signature moment as a catalogue pick
nodes.description: Treating the identity-carrying choice as a generic pick is the root homogenisation mechanism.

nodes.label: Independent picks for derived values
nodes.description: Independently chosen scales and states are why coherence collapses; enforcement is structural, not documentary.

nodes.label: A commit per save
nodes.description: Thousands of commits per session makes history useless exactly when it is needed; durability belongs to the op log.

nodes.label: Raw patch over the wire
nodes.description: An arbitrary pointer operation could rewrite the system lock or inject an override path; nearly as dangerous as raw paths.

nodes.label: Encoded document blob in browser storage
nodes.description: An in-estate precedent that does not scale to a multi-page site and hides the document from every other tool.

nodes.label: A backgrounded task treated as a server
nodes.description: It binds, answers once, and is terminated at the turn boundary.

nodes.label: Same-turn success treated as liveness
nodes.description: Proving a bind is not proving survival; only a later separate call proves it.

nodes.label: Hard aesthetic blocking after a human choice
nodes.description: Blocking a deliberate taste decision contradicts the premise the product exists to serve.

nodes.label: Claiming accessibility conformance
nodes.description: Automated tooling catches a minority of real issues, so any conformance claim is unsupportable.

nodes.label: Treating the prompt as the build artifact
nodes.description: Generation is non-deterministic, so re-deriving a system from a stored prompt cannot reproduce it.

nodes.label: Copy-and-strip export
nodes.description: The first-party precedent required hand-rewriting links and hand-excluding development pages.

nodes.label: Auto-height preview frame
nodes.description: Viewport-height rules resolve against the expanded frame, so a hero is approved at a height no device has.

nodes.label: Derived value
nodes.description: A value computed from the direction vector plus seed tables, exposing no editor control.

nodes.label: Identity vector
nodes.description: The hash-bearing set of varying direction slots; direction-bound authored artefacts sit outside it and are validated against it.

nodes.label: Validity list
nodes.description: The per-direction set of legal options for a repickable row; anything outside it is hidden rather than warned.

nodes.label: Per-run terminator
nodes.description: A random end token that makes a truncated payload detectable rather than plausible.

nodes.label: Freeze (element-level)
nodes.description: The element protection verb, deliberately distinct from the terminal publish verb to avoid two lock concepts.

nodes.label: Coherence debt
nodes.description: Recorded off-system values accepted deliberately, counted and surfaced rather than silently absorbed.

nodes.label: Flow fallback
nodes.description: The authored placement a free-positioned node returns to below the demotion width.

nodes.label: Cost class
nodes.description: A per-container-kind classification driving the motion concurrency caps.

nodes.label: Negative constraint
nodes.description: A prior identity expressed as something to avoid rather than something to reuse.

nodes.label: Launcher rung
nodes.description: One step of the fallback ladder for starting a surviving local process, ordered by how much stays in the standing language.

nodes.label: Re-attach
nodes.description: Reconnecting to an already-running recorded server instead of launching a second one after a context clear.

nodes.label: Artwork lanes
nodes.description: Code-drawn, asset-ingested and externally-generated artwork paths, honestly labelled so a single paste never implies site art.
